LIVED IN PORTLAND.
According to a special dispatch to
The Times from Portland, Mrs. Car-
ter was a resident of that city for
about four years and left Oregon for
Los Angeles in June, 1914.
For a time she owned the Bradford
Hotel, now the Ackley, later selling
that and buying the Alma. at Twelfth
and Burnside streets, Portland. Mrs.
Carter sold the Alma in August, 1913,
but, owing to the inability of the pur-
chaser ta Hive up to the contract, she
had to take ft over again. She sold
the place again in June, 1914.
C. A. Marsch of Portland was Mrs,
Carter's attorney while she was there,
and has had charge of her affairs here
since. He said last night that Mrs.
Carter still owned property in Port-
land in the shape of improved real
estate and lots.
J. L. Carter, husband of Mrs. Car-
ter, wan employed at the Waldorf in
Portland for some time, At the time
she left that city he accompanied her
to Los Angeles.
IN LONG BEACH.

‘W. H. Warren was married, accord-
ing to Long Beach accounts, While
conducting the now celebrated “social
vagrant” investigations there Jast fal!
he stated that his wife was in Port-
land.
The fact that he had a wife came
out forcibly in the course of the trial
of Herbert N. Lowe, charged with
vagrancy, and Warren's actions at
that time showed his temper and ¢x-
cltability.
Attorney Roland Swaffield, for Mr.
Lowe, was questioning Warren, who
was on the stand, in an endeavor to
learn something about his past life.
A question by the attorney caused
Warren to put his hand on his gun,
kept in a hip pocket, and defy the
lawyer to speak other than respect-
fully of Mrs, Warren. Mr. Swafiield,
who had not mentioned and did not
know of Warren‘s wife, then demand-
ed that the witness's gun be taken
from him, and it was laid on the
bench of the police judge.
W. H. Warren and B. C. Brown ar-
rived in Long Beach August 10 last,
and were engaged by the seaside city’s
Police Commission to operate in the
bath-house and elsewhere in running
down “social vagrants" They uncov-
ered the famous “606 Club." They
continued work untll October 1, when
they came to Los Angeles, belng re-
called to Long Reach for the trial of
Mr. Lowe November 12 last.
